item.text:
## 2B.2 Research Note: Narendra Modi in 2024

**Assessment:** I found **no reliable 2024 evidence** that Modi initiated or expanded a war of choice, annexation, proxy conflict, or covert destabilization beyond defensive necessity. The best-supported 2024 record is the opposite: repeated diplomacy on Ukraine, humanitarian framing, and a public commitment to peace. The main counterweight is continued strategic engagement with Russia, but that is not itself evidence of war expansion.

### Accepted claims

- **Title:** [Prime Minister Narendra Modi speaks with President Zelenskyy](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2015753&lang=2&reg=48)  
  **Publisher:** Prime Minister’s Office / PIB  
  **Date:** 20 Mar 2024  
  **URL:** https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2015753&lang=2&reg=48  
  **Claim-level summary:** Modi said India’s approach was “people-centric” and called for dialogue and diplomacy as the way forward in the Russia-Ukraine war, adding that India would do everything within its means to support a peaceful solution. This is direct evidence **against** war-of-choice behavior and **for** de-escalation.  
  **Question IDs:** 2B.2, 2B.1, 1B.1, 1B.8

- **Title:** [India-Ukraine Joint Statement on the Visit of Prime Minister of India to Ukraine](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2048245)  
  **Publisher:** Prime Minister’s Office / PIB  
  **Date:** 23 Aug 2024  
  **URL:** https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2048245  
  **Claim-level summary:** The joint statement says both leaders supported a comprehensive, just, and lasting peace based on dialogue, diplomacy, and international law, and India reiterated its principled position on peaceful resolution. This is strong evidence that Modi did **not** justify prolonging war or coercion; he instead used a diplomatic track.  
  **Question IDs:** 2B.2, 2B.1, 1B.1, 1B.8

- **Title:** [Prime Minister’s meeting with the President of Ukraine](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2048240)  
  **Publisher:** Prime Minister’s Office / PIB  
  **Date:** 23 Aug 2024  
  **URL:** https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2048240  
  **Claim-level summary:** Modi’s Kyiv visit included multiple cooperation agreements and explicit dialogue on global issues of mutual interest. While not a war-termination treaty, it is evidence of **active diplomatic engagement** rather than cross-border coercion.  
  **Question IDs:** 2B.2, 2B.1, 1B.8

- **Title:** [Prime Minister Narendra Modi speaks with President Putin](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2049059)  
  **Publisher:** Prime Minister’s Office / PIB  
  **Date:** 27 Aug 2024  
  **URL:** https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2049059  
  **Claim-level summary:** Modi emphasized dialogue, diplomacy, and practical engagement among all stakeholders to achieve an abiding and peaceful resolution. This supports the view that he sought **peaceful settlement rather than war prolongation**.  
  **Question IDs:** 2B.2, 2B.1, 1B.1, 1B.8

- **Title:** [Prime Minister’s meeting with the President of Ukraine](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2058086&lang=1&reg=3)  
  **Publisher:** Prime Minister’s Office / PIB  
  **Date:** 24 Sep 2024  
  **URL:** https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2058086&lang=1&reg=3  
  **Claim-level summary:** Modi reiterated India’s “clear, consistent and constructive approach” in favor of peaceful resolution through diplomacy and dialogue, and said India remained open to support a lasting and peaceful settlement. This is the strongest 2024 evidence against war-of-choice behavior.  
  **Question IDs:** 2B.2, 2B.1, 1B.1, 1B.8

### Countervailing / weakly negative evidence

- **Title:** [Leaders’ Joint Statement on the development of strategic areas of Russia-India economic cooperation for the period up to 2030](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2031942&lang=2&reg=48)  
  **Publisher:** Prime Minister’s Office / PIB  
  **Date:** 9 Jul 2024  
  **URL:** https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2031942&lang=2&reg=48  
  **Claim-level summary:** Modi and Putin reaffirmed the Russia-India strategic partnership and sought to deepen bilateral cooperation. This is **not evidence of war expansion**, but it does show Modi sustaining alignment with a belligerent nuclear power rather than severing ties.  
  **Question IDs:** 2B.2, 1B.1, 1B.8

- **Title:** [Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi speaks with President Putin](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleseDetailm.aspx?PRID=1996327)  
  **Publisher:** Prime Minister’s Office / PIB  
  **Date:** 15 Jan 2024  
  **URL:** https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleseDetailm.aspx?PRID=1996327  
  **Claim-level summary:** Modi agreed to further strengthen the India-Russia special and privileged strategic partnership and backed Russia’s BRICS presidency. Again, this is **strategic engagement**, not direct proof of war-of-choice conduct, but it is the closest 2024 counterweight.  
  **Question IDs:** 2B.2, 1B.1

### Search gap

- I found **no 2024 evidence** that Modi initiated annexation, covert destabilization, proxy warfare, or any equivalent war of choice.
- I found **no reliable 2024 evidence** that he used force as the preferred instrument over defensive necessity.
- The only adverse material is **continued political-strategic alignment with Russia** and campaign rhetoric elsewhere in the record; neither rises to proof of a war of choice.

### Bottom line

The best-supported conclusion is **no clear 2B.2 violation in 2024**. Modi’s public record that year is dominated by **peace-seeking diplomacy on Ukraine**, not expansion of war or covert conflict.
